correctness.rationale: The Pappus graph is defined by 18 indexed vertices and a six-periodic LCF chord sequence. Complete matching recursion produces 42 perfect matchings, partitioned into 36 Hamiltonian complements and six three-hexagon complements, whose complete edge-index sets are supplied. Each normal matching belongs to one factorization; each exceptional matching belongs to four, giving 20 total factorizations by double counting. Direct check of those six sets establishes exactly two all-exceptional triples and 18 other states with exactly one exceptional matching. Legal flips in a three-hexagon complement form K4; a Hamiltonian complementary flip is just a global colour permutation. Thus six K4 intersect three at each of two hubs, establishing precisely two copies of the cone over three triangles and all metric consequences. The matching and direct colour-search checkers are separate exhaustive implementations, both executed successfully on the actual files. No extrapolation is involved.

Abreu–Labbate–Sheehan arxiv:1002.1891v1 Theorem 3.1 explicitly covers Pappus pseudo-2-factor isomorphism: all its 2-factors have the same parity of number of cycles, but it does not enumerate the individual matching complements or Kempe moves.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The large-coverage 2021 study dominates the bare question of how many classes can occur and could algorithmically recover the component count for Pappus. Therefore two components is treated as known-in-principle, not an independent novelty claim. Aggregated class numbers do not imply a three-tetrahedra-cone structure or the location of the unique hubs. The stronger reported result is an exact isomorphism type. The 2010 pseudo-2-factor property restricts cycle parity but cannot imply the six exceptional matchings or the windmill Kempe adjacency.

originality.rationale: The novelty scope is narrowed to the complete isomorphism type of the unlabelled Pappus edge-Kempe reconfiguration graph and its exceptional-matching decomposition, not the definition of the operation, the raw factorization count or the bare number of components. Earlier arxiv:1002.1891 (2010) establishes Pappus pseudo-2-factor isomorphism (cycle-count parity, not a reconfiguration adjacency graph). Closest edge-switching studies are arxiv:1209.1730 (2012) and arxiv:2105.01363 (2021), the latter providing stronger generic enumeration coverage for mere class counts but not the claimed Pappus-specific adjacency graph, clique intersections or metric. Targeted searches for Tait, one-factorization, Pappus aliases and windmill structures found no exact antecedent. This remains a best-knowledge claim with documented risk of inaccessible specialised tables or unindexed results.
residual_risks: The 2010 Pappus paper refers to an earlier original 2008 proof of pseudo-2-factor isomorphism; the old parity fact is acknowledged, not claimed. Other historical parity studies may contain extra unpublished enumeration data.
The broad computational study of all small cubic graphs may have unpublished per-graph switching data; its published aggregate tables do not state the Pappus windmill decomposition.
An unindexed historical list of one-factorizations or obscure paper may already contain an equivalent full adjacency classification.
The graph-specific finite exact classification has no claimed extension to arbitrary cubic graphs or named palettes.

value.rationale: The Pappus graph is a canonical highly symmetric cubic bipartite graph. Its nonplanarity allows nontrivial edge-Kempe sectors unlike the planar bipartite one-class theorem. The exact two-windmill decomposition resolves not just disconnectedness but every legal one-step adjacency, the unique central factorizations in each sector, all shortest-path distances and the 54 extremal distance-two pairs. The mechanism of six exceptional one-factors whose complementary two-factors split into three hexagons explains a nonobvious reconfiguration geometry. A natural complete finite classification is useful as an exact benchmark, not an arbitrary slice or mere count of states.
